detail:
NIDDK describes clinical trials for interstitial cystitis as part of medical research looking for new ways to prevent, detect, or treat the condition and improve quality of life. The institute notes that clinical trials and other clinical studies involve volunteer participants, and that federally funded studies that are open and recruiting can be viewed through ClinicalTrials.gov.

According to NIDDK, researchers are studying many aspects of IC, including new non-drug treatments, the relationship between IC and the gut microbiome, and how to target treatments for IC based on symptoms. Sources present these as areas under active investigation, and the treatments studied in trials are described as investigational rather than established care.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about interstitial cystitis research and clinical trials.
sourceName: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
summary: NIDDK outlines IC clinical trial research, including new non-drug treatments, the relationship between IC and the gut microbiome, and matching treatments to symptom patterns.
takeaways: clinical trials test new ways to prevent, detect, or treat IC
research includes non-drug treatments and the gut microbiome
matching treatments to symptom patterns is an active research direction
title: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome: where clinical trial research is heading
